package_info.package_versions: all published versions as of April 24th, 2023
package_info.why_malicious: The packages contain heavily obfuscated code that, upon import, monkey-patches core JavaScript built-in methods (sessionStorage.getItem, Array.prototype.includes, Array.prototype.filter, JSON.stringify) to introduce random, non-deterministic, and unpredictable behavior. This deliberate sabotage undermines the reliability and security of any application that uses them. The use of obfuscation and the lack of legitimate use cases for such modifications are strong indicators of malicious intent.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code monkey-patches sessionStorage.getItem, intercepts all calls to this method, and with a 5% probability reverses the returned string, resulting in random corruption of session data retrieval.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Altering a core browser storage API to randomly corrupt returned data is highly suspicious, as it can break application logic, cause data loss, and mask further malicious activity. The obfuscation and lack of legitimate rationale further indicate intent to deceive.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: sessionStorage.getItem is expected to return the exact value stored for a given key. Introducing random reversals violates the deterministic contract of this API and can cause unpredictable application behavior.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Such modifications might be used in controlled testing environments for chaos engineering, but never in production code or without explicit documentation and user consent.
key_indicators: Randomized string reversal in returned values
Obfuscated code structure targeting browser storage APIs

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code monkey-patches Array.prototype.includes, intercepts all inclusion checks, and forces the method to always return false for arrays of odd length, causing incorrect and unpredictable inclusion results.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Modifying a fundamental array method to behave incorrectly based on array length is a classic sabotage technique that undermines application logic and data integrity. This can introduce subtle, hard-to-diagnose bugs.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Array.prototype.includes should accurately determine element presence regardless of array length. Forcing false results for odd-length arrays breaks this contract and can cause logic errors.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: No legitimate use in production. Such behavior might only be used in explicit chaos testing scenarios with clear warnings and user consent.
key_indicators: Conditional logic based on array length to alter return value
Obfuscated or non-standard code modifying core array methods

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code monkey-patches Array.prototype.filter, intercepts all filter operations, and on Sundays with a 10% probability removes one element from the result, introducing time-based and random data loss.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Introducing random, time-based data loss in a core array method is highly disruptive and can cause subtle, hard-to-debug errors in applications relying on deterministic filtering.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Array.prototype.filter should return a deterministic subset of the array based solely on the filter function. Randomly dropping elements based on the day of the week and probability violates this expectation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: No legitimate use in production. Such behavior might be used in chaos engineering with explicit user consent and clear documentation.
key_indicators: Time-based (day of week) and probabilistic logic to alter results
Randomized removal of elements from filter results

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code monkey-patches JSON.stringify, intercepts all serialization calls, and with a 10% probability replaces all uppercase 'I' characters with lowercase 'l' in the output, corrupting serialized data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Corrupting serialized data output by randomly altering characters can break APIs, cause data loss, and introduce subtle bugs that are difficult to trace, especially when the corruption is probabilistic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: JSON.stringify should produce a faithful, deterministic string representation of the input object. Randomly replacing characters in the output violates this expectation and can cause downstream failures.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: No legitimate use in production. Such modifications might only be used for deliberate error injection in controlled testing environments with explicit user awareness.
key_indicators: Randomized string corruption in serialized output
Obfuscated code targeting core serialization functions

attack_chain.action: Upon import, the package immediately monkey-patches core JavaScript built-in methods (sessionStorage.getItem, Array.prototype.includes, Array.prototype.filter, JSON.stringify) to introduce random, non-deterministic behavior into standard library functions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Any code in the application that relies on these built-in methods will behave unpredictably, leading to data corruption, logic errors, and hard-to-debug issues that undermine application reliability and security.

behavioral_signatures: Monkey-patching of core JavaScript built-in methods (sessionStorage.getItem, Array.prototype.includes, Array.prototype.filter, JSON.stringify) at import-time
Introduction of random or probabilistic behavior into standard library functions
Obfuscated or minified code present in the main entry point (index.js)
file_indicators: index.js containing obfuscated or minified code
Assignments or redefinitions of sessionStorage.getItem, Array.prototype.includes, Array.prototype.filter, or JSON.stringify
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Perform static analysis on package entry points (such as index.js) to detect monkey-patching or reassignment of core JavaScript built-in methods (sessionStorage.getItem, Array.prototype.includes, Array.prototype.filter, JSON.stringify). Flag any package that introduces random or probabilistic behavior into these methods, especially if the code is obfuscated or minified. Automated tools should look for assignments to these prototypes or global objects, and trigger code review for any such modifications without clear, documented intent.
